# Two force-refreshed upstreams rendezvous on one node

A node declaring `force_upstream_refresh: true` on two upstreams pulls both into
the frame, each runs once, and the receiver dispatches once against the full
refreshed set. The shape does not livelock.

## The template

```yaml
name: rendezvous-demo
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: never/sent
    body_schema: {type: object}
nodes:
  - type: trigger
    kind: loop_counter
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max: {type: integer, default: 9}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: left
    kind: loop_counter
    subscribes:
      - node: never/sent
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max: {type: integer, default: 9}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: right
    kind: loop_counter
    subscribes:
      - node: never/sent
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max: {type: integer, default: 9}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: receiver
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: trigger
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: left
        type: attribute/count/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: true
      - node: right
        type: attribute/count/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: true
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          from_left:  {type: integer, source: "{{nodes.left.attribute.count}}"}
          from_right: {type: integer, source: "{{nodes.right.attribute.count}}"}
```

`left` and `right` subscribe only to a message type nothing ever sends, so the
force-refresh declarations are the only thing that can run them.

## Drive it

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -d '{}'

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/node-runs?instance_id=$IID"
```

## What the product does

The operator message wakes `trigger`. The receiver's invalidation pulls both
`left` and `right` into the frame. Each runs exactly once.

The receiver dispatches exactly once, and its outcome carries both upstream
values.

The instance reaches rest with no live runs: neither upstream re-ran, and the
receiver computed from the full refreshed set rather than looping.
